title: Solved edge cases
description: The edge cases a reference repo already handles, recorded as scenario seeds rather than as documentation. This is the phase where the corpus stops being a description of four houses and starts being a specification of what Open House has to survive: a flaky device, a restart, a false trigger, notification spam and an unavailable sensor are all handled in at least one of the four setups, and each solution is a guard the product has to have or an argument for not having it.

scenario.description: What goes wrong, in our own words. Never a quotation from a source repo: the guard below is read from the config, but the description of what it protects against is ours, and two of the four repos grant no reuse of their prose.

guard.description: What the repo does about it, in our own words. The requirement asks for the guard used; recording it as a description rather than as the YAML that implements it is what keeps this file out of the prose gate's way.

repo.description: The repo the guard was found in.

phase_1.description: The Phase 1 placeholder this seed becomes. Required and non-empty: a seed with no placeholder is a note nobody will act on, and it is the one field that makes this file a work item rather than a reading list.
